top_temples.name: Dimapur Kalibari
top_temples.location_note: Built in 1956; one of Dimapur's oldest and best-known Hindu temples, active site for Durga Puja and other major festivals.

top_temples.name: Dimapur Jain Temple
top_temples.location_note: Built in 1947 by Jain families who relocated from Kohima; known for its architecture and stained-glass work.

top_temples.name: Lakshmi Narayan Temple
top_temples.location_note: A central Hindu worship site in Dimapur, known for its annual Rath Yatra celebration.

top_temples.name: ISKCON Temple, Dimapur
top_temples.location_note: Local branch of the ISKCON movement, offers deity worship and spiritual programs.

top_temples.name: Mandir, 41 Assam Rifles, Kiphire
top_temples.deity: General/garrison worship (no single primary deity documented)
top_temples.location_note: Small temple within the 41 Assam Rifles camp at Kiphire, serving the paramilitary garrison and local Hindu community; confirmed via a 2025 Nagaland government (DIPR) incident report.

top_temples.name: Durga Bari Mandir
top_temples.deity: Durga (with subsidiary Kali and Shiva shrines)
top_temples.location_note: PWD Colony, Kohima; a focal point for the local Hindu community, blends traditional Hindu design with local architectural influences.

top_temples.name: Jain Temple, Kohima
top_temples.location_note: Built in 1920 by eight Sethi families; the oldest Jain temple in Nagaland, Digambar sect, has its own Wikipedia entry.

top_temples.name: Nepali Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Gathering place for Kohima's Nepali/Gorkha community for worship and cultural festivals.

top_temples.name: Gorkha Singhadevi Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Chandmari, Kohima; dates to the 1880s, one of the oldest Hindu temples in the city, tied to early Gorkha settlement history.

top_temples.name: Radha Krishna Temple, Kohima
top_temples.location_note: Tekhuba, Phesama area of Kohima; serves the local Hindu community.

top_temples.name: Wokha Shiv Mandir
top_temples.location_note: On DC Hill, Kohima-Mokokchung Road, Wokha; built 1975, though locals trace worship at the site back to a 1942 account of a Shivlingam found in the ground. Popular during Mahashivratri.

top_temples.name: Kali Mandir, Wokha
top_temples.location_note: Wokha town; second major Hindu shrine in the town, active during Kali Puja.
